title: Manti remains out of reach
summary: The Nephites cannot draw the Lamanites from Manti’s strongholds or attack their much larger force. They must maintain their regained lands and wait for reinforcements and provisions.

explicit_facts.text: The Nephites’ next objective is to obtain Manti, but they cannot decoy the Lamanites away from their strongholds.
The Lamanites greatly outnumber the Nephite army, which dares not attack their strongholds.
The Nephites must maintain regained lands and wait for strength and provisions from Zarahemla.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A fortified city and a comparatively small Nephite force may be shown to suggest the stated disparity.
unspecified_visual_details: The fortifications’ appearance, landscape, clothing, and the precise location of the army are not described.

narration.text: there was no way that we could lead them out of the city

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The narration reports the strategic situation; no battle occurs in this moment.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a decoy attempt or an assault on the strongholds.

title: An embassy and a wait
summary: The narrator sends an embassy to the governor to report the people’s affairs. The narrator’s group waits for provisions and strength from Zarahemla. Meanwhile, the Lamanites receive strength and provisions, so the wait profits the group little.
locations: Unspecified location where the narrator’s group waits

explicit_facts.text: The narrator sends an embassy to the governor of their land to acquaint him with the people’s affairs.
The narrator’s group waits for provisions and strength from Zarahemla.
The Lamanites also receive strength and provisions from day to day, and the wait profits the narrator’s group little.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The embassy may be shown departing; its route and destination setting are not specified.
The narrator’s group may be shown waiting, without depicting the Lamanites’ reported activity as part of the same scene.
unspecified_visual_details: The location, embassy members’ identities, and means of communication are unspecified.
The governor’s appearance and the nature of the expected provisions are unspecified.

narration.text: I thus did send an embassy to the governor of our land, to acquaint him concerning the affairs of our people.
we did wait to receive provisions and strength from the land of Zarahemla.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Lamanites’ receipt of strength and provisions is reported context, not a separate event to stage in this scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the governor receiving the embassy or invent its message or any spoken words.
Do not show the expected provisions or reinforcements arriving.

title: Raids and prolonged hardship
summary: The Lamanites make intermittent sorties, but the Nephites cannot bring them to battle because of their retreats and strongholds. The Nephites wait for many months and nearly perish from hunger.

explicit_facts.text: The Lamanites sally against the Nephites from time to time, and the Nephites cannot engage them because of their retreats and strongholds.
The Nephites wait in difficult circumstances for many months, nearly perishing from lack of food.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The waiting soldiers may appear strained; no specific physical condition is stated.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting, number and outcome of individual sorties, and the soldiers’ precise condition are not specified.

narration.text: we did wait in these difficult circumstances for the space of many months

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The sorties and months of waiting are reported events; do not combine them into a single attack.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show a battle or depict starvation with graphic bodily effects.

title: Food arrives with two thousand men
summary: Food reaches the Nephites guarded by an army of two thousand men. Helaman describes this as all the assistance they received to defend themselves and their country.

explicit_facts.text: The Nephites receive food guarded by an army of two thousand men.
This is all the assistance they receive to defend themselves and their country against an innumerable enemy.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The food and its armed escort may be shown arriving together.
unspecified_visual_details: The kind and quantity of food, the escort’s appearance, and the precise place of arrival are unspecified.

narration.text: we did receive food, which was guarded to us by an army of two thousand men

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The number of escorting men is stated; the enemy’s innumerability is a narrative description, not a visible count.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent additional reinforcements or depict the food’s source beyond what is stated.

title: Fear and prayer
summary: Not knowing why more reinforcements were not sent, the Nephites grieve and fear destruction. They pray for strength, deliverance, and the ability to retain their cities, lands, and possessions.

explicit_facts.text: The Nephites do not know why more strength was not sent and fear that God’s judgments may bring their overthrow and destruction.
They pray for strength, deliverance, and help retaining their cities, lands, and possessions.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The Nephites may be shown praying together; no particular posture is specified.
unspecified_visual_details: The precise setting, number of people praying, and any visible divine response are not specified here.

narration.text: we did pour out our souls in prayer to God

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The fear of divine judgments is reported as the Nephites’ concern.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict an actual judgment or a visible appearance of God in this moment.

title: Assurance and renewed courage
summary: The Lord visits the Nephites with assurances of deliverance, peace, faith, and hope. They take courage with their small force and resolve to conquer their enemies and maintain their lands, possessions, families, and liberty.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord visits the Nephites with assurances, speaks peace to their souls, and grants faith and hope for deliverance.
The Nephites take courage with their small force and resolve to conquer their enemies and maintain their lands, possessions, families, and liberty.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The Nephites may be shown taking heart together; the source does not describe a visible form of the Lord.
unspecified_visual_details: The manner of the Lord’s assurance, the setting, and any visible sign are unspecified.

narration.text: he did speak peace to our souls

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The assurance and peace are described spiritually; no visible divine appearance is stated.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Lord visibly or add spoken words beyond the source’s account.

title: The Nephites camp near Manti
summary: The Nephites advance against the Lamanites in Manti and pitch tents beside the wilderness near the city. The next day, the Lamanites send spies around them to assess their number and strength.

explicit_facts.text: The Nephites go against the Lamanites in Manti and pitch tents by the wilderness near the city.
On the following day, the Lamanites send spies around the Nephites to discover their number and strength.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The camp and nearby city may be visible in the same landscape; the spies may be positioned around the camp.
unspecified_visual_details: The city’s appearance, the spies’ number, and the camps’ layout are unspecified.

narration.text: we did pitch our tents by the wilderness side

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The spying takes place the next day after the Nephites camp.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a Lamanite attack in this scene.

title: Preparations and Concealment
summary: The Lamanites begin preparing to come out to battle. The narrator has Gid and a small group hide in the wilderness, and Teomner and a small group do likewise. Gid's group is on the right, the other on the left, while the narrator remains with the rest of his army where they first pitched their tents.
characters: The narrator and the remainder of his army
locations: Place where the narrator's army first pitched its tents

explicit_facts.text: The Lamanites begin preparing to come out to battle after seeing that the narrator's force is not strong in numbers.
The narrator causes Gid and a small number of men, and Teomner and a small number of men, to hide in the wilderness.
Gid and his men are on the right, the others are on the left, and the narrator remains with the rest of his army where they first pitched their tents.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The two concealed groups can be shown in separate parts of the wilderness, with the remaining army at its original campsite.
unspecified_visual_details: The groups' precise distances, the terrain, and the Lamanites' preparations are not described.

narration.text: Now Gid and his men were on the right and the others on the left;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The passage describes preparations and concealment, not a battle taking place.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a battle or add dialogue.
Do not identify the narrator by a name absent from these verses.
Do not invent a location name or biographical details for the groups.

title: The Nephites retreat into the wilderness
summary: The Lamanite army advances against the Nephites. As the Lamanites are about to attack with swords, Helaman orders his men to retreat into the wilderness. The Lamanites pursue, and the Nephites pass between the concealed groups without exposing them.

explicit_facts.text: The Lamanites come out with a numerous army, and Helaman’s men retreat into the wilderness as the Lamanites are about to attack with swords.
The Lamanites pursue at speed into the wilderness, and the Nephites pass between Gid and Teomner without the Lamanites discovering them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The retreating Nephites may be shown moving between the concealed groups as pursuers follow.
unspecified_visual_details: The exact route, spacing, and appearance of the wilderness are unspecified.

narration.text: I caused that my men, those who were with me, should retreat into the wilderness

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Lamanites are about to attack at the start of the retreat; do not show the attack landing.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict sword wounds, casualties, or the discovery of Gid’s and Teomner’s groups.

title: Gid and Teomner seize the city
summary: After the Lamanite army passes, Gid and Teomner rise from hiding and cut off the Lamanite spies. They run to Manti, attack the guards left there, destroy them, and take possession of the city while most of the Lamanite army is away.

explicit_facts.text: After the Lamanite army passes, Gid and Teomner rise from hiding and cut off the Lamanite spies so they cannot return to the city.
Gid and Teomner run to the city, attack the guards, destroy them, and take possession of the city.
The Lamanites had allowed their whole army, except a few guards, to be led into the wilderness.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Gid and Teomner’s groups may be shown entering a city defended by only a few guards.
unspecified_visual_details: The number of spies and guards, and the visual details of the city and combat, are unspecified.

narration.text: Gid and Teomner did rise up from their secret places

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The reported combat can be shown without gore.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict wounds, blood, or severed body parts.

title: Two armies take different routes
summary: Gid and Teomner have obtained the Lamanite strongholds. Helaman’s army travels through the wilderness toward Zarahemla. Seeing the Nephites march that way, the Lamanites fear a trap and retreat by the route they came.

explicit_facts.text: Gid and Teomner obtain possession of the Lamanite strongholds.
After traveling much in the wilderness, Helaman’s army takes its course toward Zarahemla.
The Lamanites see the Nephites marching toward Zarahemla, fear a plan to destroy them, and retreat into the wilderness by their former route.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The Nephite and Lamanite movements may be shown as separate forces on different routes within the wilderness.
unspecified_visual_details: The distance between the armies, precise routes, and appearance of the terrain are unspecified.

narration.text: they began to retreat into the wilderness again

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Lamanites’ fear is reported, not shown as a visible event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Lamanite retreat and the Nephite arrival at Manti as simultaneous.

title: Night march toward Manti
summary: At night, the Lamanite chief captains camp, supposing the Nephites weary and unaware of danger to Manti. Helaman keeps his men awake and sends them by another way toward Manti. By the next day, the Nephites are beyond the Lamanites and reach Manti first.

explicit_facts.text: At night, the Lamanites pitch tents, believing the Nephites weary and supposing their whole army has been driven away; they do not consider Manti.
Helaman orders his men not to sleep but to march at night by another route toward Manti.
By the following day, the Nephites are beyond the Lamanites and arrive before them at Manti.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The separate night movements may be conveyed through distinct moments: Lamanites camp, then Nephites march.
unspecified_visual_details: The route, weather, camp arrangement, and distance traveled are unspecified.

narration.text: I caused that my men should not sleep

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Lamanite camp and the Nephite night march are separate actions in the same night.
prohibited_inventions: Do not collapse the nighttime camp and the next-day arrival into one moment.

title: Manti taken without bloodshed
summary: The Nephites take possession of Manti without bloodshed. When the Lamanite armies arrive near the city and see the Nephites ready to meet them, they are astonished and afraid and flee into the wilderness.

explicit_facts.text: The Nephites take possession of Manti by stratagem without shedding blood.
The Lamanite armies arrive near Manti, see the Nephites prepared to meet them, and flee into the wilderness in fear.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The Nephites may be shown positioned to defend the city as the Lamanite army turns away.
unspecified_visual_details: The city’s defenses, the precise stratagem, and the armies’ formations are unspecified.

narration.text: we did take possession of the city of Manti without the shedding of blood

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The taking of the city and the later flight of the Lamanites are distinct moments.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict bloodshed or casualties in the capture of Manti.

title: Lamanites flee with captives
summary: The Lamanites flee from the quarter of the land, carrying many women and children away. The recaptured cities are in Nephite possession, and families return home except those taken prisoner. Helaman notes the small size of the armies relative to the many cities they must maintain.

explicit_facts.text: The Lamanite armies flee the quarter of the land, carrying many women and children away.
The cities taken by the Lamanites are in Nephite possession; fathers, women, and children return home except those carried off as prisoners.
The Nephite armies are small for maintaining so many cities and possessions.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The flight with captives and the return of families may be represented as separate moments, not one simultaneous scene.
unspecified_visual_details: The identities of captives and returnees, exact places, and number of cities are unspecified.

narration.text: our fathers and our women and our children are returning to their homes

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The return is reported as occurring at the time of Helaman’s account.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the captives as willingly accompanying the Lamanites or invent personal identities.

title: Trust Amid Uncertainty
summary: Helaman reports that his group has obtained its cities and lands. They do not know why the government has not sent more strength. He considers possible explanations without establishing either one and expresses trust that God will deliver them.
characters: Men who came up unto the group

explicit_facts.text: Helaman says his group has obtained cities and lands that were their own and credits God with giving them victory.
Neither his group nor the men who came up unto them know why they have not received greater strength.
He raises the possibility that the recipients have drawn forces to another quarter of the land; he does not establish that this happened.
He fears that a faction in the government may be withholding assistance; he does not establish that such a faction exists.
He trusts that God will deliver them despite the weakness of their armies.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The first-person report can be presented without staging the reported victory or either proposed explanation.
unspecified_visual_details: Helaman’s appearance, immediate setting, and the report’s physical form are unspecified.

spoken_dialogue.text: But behold, we trust in our God who has given us victory over those lands,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Helaman

spoken_dialogue.text: Now we do not know the cause that the government does not grant us more strength;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Helaman

spoken_dialogue.text: But, behold, it mattereth not—we trust God will deliver us, notwithstanding the weakness of our armies,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Helaman

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The diversion of forces and the possible government faction remain uncertainties, not established events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not add “I am Helaman, the son of Alma.” as a quotation; it does not appear in the supplied verses.
Do not stage either proposed explanation as fact or depict the reported victory as a new present-tense event.

title: Helaman closes his report
summary: Helaman dates his report to the end of the twenty-ninth year: the Nephites possess their lands and the Lamanites have fled to Nephi. The sons of the people of Ammon are with him in Manti; none has been slain, though many have wounds. Helaman describes their steadfast faith and closes his epistle to Moroni with a prayer for the people.

explicit_facts.text: At the end of the twenty-ninth year, the Nephites possess their lands and the Lamanites have fled to the land of Nephi.
The sons of the people of Ammon are with Helaman in Manti; none has been slain.
They have received many wounds, stand fast in liberty, remember the Lord, keep his commandments, and have faith in prophecies concerning the future.
Helaman addresses Moroni as his beloved brother, prays for the Lord to keep him and favor the people, and closes his epistle, identifying himself as Helaman, son of Alma.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The sons of the people of Ammon may be shown in Manti; their wounds may be indicated without gore.
unspecified_visual_details: Their individual identities, the appearance of any wounds, and whether Moroni is physically present are unspecified.

narration.text: even one soul has not been slain

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Helaman’s words to Moroni are part of an epistle, not a face-to-face speech.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show Moroni present in Manti or invent a visual appearance for him.
